summary: The current JS replay enters js/dothrow.js:hurtle_step’s unseen-monster branch through mhitu.js:hitmu and uhitm.js:mhitm_knockback, then throws TypeError: map_invisible() draws to the global game at js/dothrow.js:981. C display.c:map_invisible updates remembered glyph state and paints the live display; JS passes a cloned planning state to the live-only helper even though map_invisible_planning already provides the memory-only behavior. The fresh replay confirms the exception, but the returned trace does not localize it to a normalized input step; C step 135 is only a possible hurtle route, not a proven correspondence.

source.branch: In hurtle_step, after movement reaches an occupied square, wake the monster; if canspotmon is false, C calls map_invisible for that square. In the JS planning clone, preserve the clone memory write without drawing through the module-global live game.

evidence: C source path: mhitu.c:hitmu (1144 onward) calls uhitm.c:mhitm_knockback (1193); uhitm.c:mhitm_knockback can call dothrow.c:hurtle; dothrow.c:hurtle calls walk_path; dothrow.c:hurtle_step (773 onward) checks the destination with m_at, wakes an occupied monster, then calls display.c:map_invisible when !canspotmon (dothrow.c:867–868). display.c:map_invisible (378–384) writes GLYPH_INVISIBLE when hero_memory is enabled and calls show_glyph for the live display.

JS source path: js/dothrow.js:hurtle_step receives state and planning at lines 879–886; after m_at finds a monster, the invisible branch at lines 961–982 calls map_invisible(mon.mx, mon.my, state) without selecting by planning. js/display.js:map_invisible rejects state !== game at lines 3432–3435; the existing map_invisible_planning helper at lines 3444–3450 changes clone memory through mapInvisibleMemory without painting the global screen.

Fresh assigned-case replay at ee3dc7db5cacad4d18557379dd75b9558de8d421: run-t4LMEz executed the frozen 138-step C recording in a fresh Node process using scoring-workspace jsmain.runSegment and threw TypeError: map_invisible() draws to the global game. The stack is preserved at .cache/v21-archon-map-invisible-replay.json (SHA-256 f9376b1eaa86400bd9e048b4b99d6e9e8592934497d0b2c610212bb54f0cd74b); bounded terminal receipt .cache/v21-archon-map-invisible-run-t4LMEz.receipt.json (SHA-256 0a5350234f3b873aebcea05977b0c95817c6f37526c9441e06fcecc1d0ee9308) and stdout .cache/v21-archon-map-invisible-run-t4LMEz.stdout.log (SHA-256 9e46802234c6ad837ced08e82f391fc4c8ee0be161be004f0f6d93b604907c6c) are retained. The failed run returns no normalized JS boundary or game trace, so no input step is assigned to the exception.

C counter-evidence: the recording’s Archon radiance/hit is at normalized step 133. Knockback chance draws rn2(6)=3 at step 133 and rn2(6)=5 at step 134 return false; step 135 has rn2(3)=1 followed by rn2(6)=0, making it the first possible later hurtle path. Those C draws do not prove that the remaining hurtle gates pass, identify a collision target, or locate the JS exception at the same point.

Bounded correction scope: fix only the planning/live helper choice at js/dothrow.js:hurtle_step’s invisible-monster branch. The existing js/display.js:map_invisible_planning already represents C’s cloned-state memory write without live drawing; retain map_invisible for the live game. A83 also allows js/dothrow.js, but its current dothrow edits only rewire is_lava/sobj_at/m_in_air imports and do not touch hurtle_step; preserve those imports. A83’s contract:timeout-clone-display-rng-caller reservation concerns its timer path, not this glyph-memory branch. Reconcile imports at the clean boundary rather than expanding this finding into A83’s path.
